chapter_title: Early Humans and Beginning of Civilisation

zero_omission_notes.summary: Traces human biological and cultural evolution from early hominin origins in Africa through the Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, Neolithic, and Chalcolithic ages, culminating in urban Bronze Age civilisations like the Sindhu-Sarasvatī, Mesopotamian, Egyptian, and Chinese civilisations.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Biological evolution transitioned early primates (Australopithecines) into Homo sapiens. Homo erectus, using hand axes and cleavers, was the first hominin species to migrate out of Africa (~2 to 0.5 million years ago). Subsequent waves led to Neanderthals and modern Homo sapiens spread.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Hominin and Fossil
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Hominin: Modern humans and early human-like ancestors. Fossil: Preserved remains or impressions of ancient organisms mineralized over thousands of years.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 4.2 Stone Age Typology in Indian Subcontinent
detailed_sections.full_notes: 1) Palaeolithic: Hunter-gatherers using core/flake stone tools (hand axes, scrapers) in sites like Bhimbetka and Attirampakkam. 2) Mesolithic: Use of tiny, precise microlithic tools and cave rock art (Bhimbetka). 3) Neolithic: Beginning of farming/domestication (~7000 BCE Mehrgarh), polished tools, and settled village life.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: A UNESCO World Heritage Site in Madhya Pradesh containing hundreds of painted rock caves spanning Palaeolithic to Mesolithic periods.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Neolithic settled farming led to surplus food, metallurgy (copper + tin = bronze), writing, and urbanization. Major river valley civilisations emerged: Sindhu-Sarasvatī (Indus/Ghaggar), Mesopotamian (Tigris/Euphrates), Egyptian (Nile), and Chinese (Huang He).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Harappan Script vs Deciphered Scripts
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Harappan script (Sindhu lipi) remains undeciphered, unlike Mesopotamian Cuneiform or Egyptian Hieroglyphics.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: Archaeological Tool Classification Activity - Categorize prehistoric artifacts based on stone tool manufacturing techniques.
procedure_or_steps: Examine tool dimensions and edge chipping techniques.
Identify heavy chipped cobbles/flakes as Palaeolithic Hand Axes.
Identify geometric small blades (<3 cm) as Mesolithic Microliths.
Identify ground, smooth-edged stone axes as Neolithic Celts.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: Tools evolve from crude heavy stones to specialized small microliths, and finally polished farming tools.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Tool refinement reflects growing technological cognition and environmental adaptation.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: The major transition in human history from hunting and gathering to agriculture and animal domestication.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: The Neolithic Revolution at Mehrgarh enabled permanent pottery-making agrarian villages.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: A minute stone tool made of flint or chert, typically used as teeth on composite bone or wooden weapons.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Mesolithic hunters hafted microliths onto arrows and wooden spears.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: Palaeolithic (Old Stone) -> Mesolithic (Middle Stone) -> Neolithic (New Stone) -> Chalcolithic (Copper-Stone) -> Bronze Age
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.si_unit_or_notation: Defined by material technology used for tool production and food acquisition methods.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Classifying an site with polished stone axes and pottery as Neolithic.

textbook_exercises.question: Why do historians divide early human history into different ages such as Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age?
textbook_exercises.answer: Historians categorize prehistoric eras based on the dominant material technology used for tools, weapons, and daily implements. This material progress reflects advancements in human knowledge, pyrotechnology, trade networks, and social organization.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: Which was the first hominin species to migrate out of Africa?
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: Homo erectus possessed bipedal endurance and stone hand axes enabling migration out of Africa ~2 million years ago.

short_answer_questions.question: State two distinctive features of the Neolithic site of Mehrgarh.
short_answer_questions.answer: 1) It provides the earliest evidence of barley and wheat cultivation and sheep/goat domestication in South Asia (~7000 BCE). 2) Inhabitants lived in rectangular mud-brick houses and created early earthenware pottery. Key points: Earliest South Asian farming evidence (~7000 BCE), Mud-brick settled architecture

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Source Passage (The period before writing is understood through archaeology....): Which ancient civilisation used the cuneiform script?
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: The Mesopotamian civilisation in the Tigris-Euphrates valley.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Explain how surplus food production in the Neolithic period led to the rise of Bronze Age civilisations.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: 1) Farming innovations provided stable food surpluses. 2) Surpluses freed a portion of the population from direct food production, enabling specialization in crafts (pottery, metallurgy), administration, and trade. 3) Craft specialization spurred metallurgical advancements (smelting copper and tin into bronze). 4) Urban trade networks required record-keeping, driving script invention. 5) Centralized governance emerged to manage irrigation and trade, creating Bronze Age cities.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: Archaeologists excavating a site discover stone grinding slabs, charred wheat grains, animal bones showing domestic butchery marks, and fired clay storage jars.

qa.question: Which prehistoric era does this site belong to? Justify your choice.
qa.answer: Neolithic period. Justification: Grain cultivation (wheat), animal husbandry, grain processing tools (grinding slabs), and storage pottery are core hallmarks of Neolithic food production.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Assuming early humans lived alongside dinosaurs.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Dinosaurs went extinct ~66 million years ago, whereas early hominins emerged only ~6-7 million years ago and Homo sapiens ~300,000 years ago.
